raw_segments.text: I pulled the string of the whistle, and I did this because I saw the pilgrims on deck
getting out their rifles with an air of anticipating a jolly lark.
At the sudden screech there was a movement of abject terror through that wedged mass
Don't—don't you frighten them away, cried someone on deck disconsolately.
I pulled the string time after time.
They broke and ran, they leaped, they crouched, they swerved, they dodged the flying terror
The three red chaps had fallen flat, face down on the shore, as though they had been
Only the barbarous and superb woman did not so much as flinch, and stretched tragically
her bare arms after us over the somber and glittering river.
